statement: In ggml_compute_forward_flash_attn_ext_f16_one_chunk, replace the per-cell aligned-run test with an outer loop over mask blocks: test each complete block once, skip wholly -inf blocks, and process remaining cells in ascending KV order. Preserve both accumulator paths, K/V reads and the use_ref walk. This targets traversal overhead and work imbalance rather than changing the barrier primitive. Unlike the retired GQA-shared-mask proposal, it shares no enumeration across heads. It is bit-exact by construction: every surviving cell executes the same dot, exp and accumulation sequence in the same order. The selected target's instrumented depth profile reports FLASH_ATTN_EXT at 32.09% wall share; this motivates testing, not a predicted gain.

Under cpu_fa_schedule, pair adjacent query heads sharing the same K/V head and interleave their updates inside one ascending KV-cell traversal, using separate per-row state within existing thread scratch. Preserve K/V read helpers, masks, sinks, overflow replay, split-KV boundaries and the use_ref walk; retain HEAD for unsupported layouts and prefill. This is bit-exact by construction: only independent rows are interleaved, and each row retains its original dot, expf and accumulator operation sequence. The hypothesis is improved K/V cache reuse. Attention is a deliberate lower-ranked choice because barrier primitives, float tile replanning and recent expert partition variants have already been answered, while current operator evidence discourages further streaming-kernel instruction tweaks. The selected sibling reports 4.70% attention wall share, so a serving gain above the floor is uncertain; long-context benefits are not claimed for these frozen requests.

In the admitted x86 IndexHelperIQ3S::make2 body in the last #else arm, replace each eight scalar iq3s_grid loads and _mm256_set_epi32 construction with _mm256_i32gather_epi32 using the existing index vector and scale 4. Preserve index generation, lane order, signs, scales and dot accumulation, making this bit-exact by construction. This targets IQ3_S expert computation that may contribute to straggler wait rather than changing the barrier primitive; five-row solo scheduling is already implemented. The original profile attributes 7.19% of sampled periods to IQ3S IQ_1, and the sibling attributes 25.45% of op wall to MUL_MAT_ID; neither implies a gain. Gather may reduce scalar extraction and vector assembly overhead. The required served-shape manifest is now present, allowing the loop to attempt the mandated ppl-contract gates.

In ggml_compute_forward_rms_norm_f32, replace the inspected serial double sum-of-squares chain with eight independent double accumulators, a fixed-order merge and a remainder loop, preserving each float square, row ownership, strides, in-place handling and fused multiplication. This exposes instruction parallelism in long rows without adding barriers or duplicating row scans. This is TOL, not bit-exact: the sum order changes. The selected sibling attributes 3.29% of op wall to RMS_NORM, so the serving payoff is bounded and may miss the floor. Higher-ranked synchronization already includes the three-row solo keep, barrier replacements are settled nulls, and the latest dense-stream evidence discourages further dot-body tweaks.

GATES-KEEP: d0a61d080ab9. In tinyBLAS_Q0_AVX::gemm4xN, restrict the existing next-tile weight prefetch to Q8_0 verify tiles with RN == 5 and k == 80, corresponding to an attested tensor contraction dimension of 2560 and five activation columns. Source inspection confirms this prefetch currently runs unconditionally between tiles. Preserve its addresses, distance and hint inside that gate; other shapes execute the pre-keep path. This targets work-balance stragglers without changing arithmetic: every output retains its existing dot and reduction order, so outputs remain bit-exact. The shape gate is a hypothesis about workload separation, not proof of model identity.

In the admitted x86 IndexHelperIQ3S::make2 implementation under #else, replace each eight-scalar iq3s_grid lookup plus _mm256_set_epi32 assembly with _mm256_i32gather_epi32 using the existing index vector and scale 4. Source inspection confirms two such assemblies per call. This targets IQ3_S codebook decoding in the selected UD model's gate/up experts, rather than the exhausted dispatch, mapping or barrier mechanisms. Preserve index construction, signs, scales and dot accumulation order, making this bit-exact by construction, while retaining the route's mandatory ppl_contract gates. The original request-scoped CPU profile is unavailable; the sibling node profile establishes MUL_MAT_ID's 26.51% wall share, but does not establish gather overhead or a predicted gain. The hypothesis is that avoiding index-vector extraction and scalar vector assembly reduces expert-kernel instruction overhead.

The dense Q8_0 verify GEMM (tinyBLAS_Q0_AVX<block_q8_0,block_q8_0,float>::gemm4xN, ggml/src/ggml-cpu/llamafile/sgemm.cpp:1524, admitted route dense_q8_tinyblas) is memory-LATENCY bound, not compute- or bandwidth-bound: its k-loop is unrolled x1 with zero prefetch (anchor DSO disassembly of gemm4xN<3>, 0x23db00-0x23dd6a: 7 unaligned 32B block loads per l-iteration, no prefetch instruction anywhere in the loop, one accumulator spilled per iteration to [rsp-0x20]), so each l-iteration stalls on the ~120-cycle load-to-use latency of its 4 weight blocks. The measured 213 GB/s wall bandwidth is exactly this structure: 4 rows x 34 B x 48 threads / 120 cycles @ 3.9 GHz = 212 GB/s. Mechanism: add 4 __builtin_prefetch calls inside the gemm4xN k-loop, one per A weight row (ii..ii+3), 8 blocks (l+8, guarded l+8<k) ahead, locality 1 — the same idiom the sibling f32 tinyBLAS class already uses at sgemm.cpp:3103-3107 (distance 1). This raises per-core in-flight weight bytes from ~136 B (one block-set) to ~1.4 KB, roughly 8x the Little's-law requirement (target BW x latency ~= 176 B/core), so blocks are fetched well before use. Expected: dense Q8_0 bandwidth 213 -> ~250-275 GB/s (half-screen ceiling), i.e. -6..-9 ms on a 101 ms cycle (dense = 40.9 ms/cycle, 8.7 GB/cycle, 42.83% of op wall) ~= +6-10% aggregate_tok_s, far above the 1.554% half-screen floor. Bit-identical by construction: prefetches have no value effect; no FP op is added, removed, or reordered; the ordering argument is that the edit is pure load-side effect. Edit is confined to the gemm4xN template body (covers RN=1..4, the live <3> and <2> specializations); added lines use the block pointer (A + lda*(ii+i) + l + 8) with no .qs/.qh member access, no header change, no other class touched.

Set OMP_PLACES to spread the 48 decode threads across both NUMA nodes (e.g. OMP_PLACES=0:96:2 with OMP_PROC_BIND=close on a 96-CPU 2-node box; equivalently any 48-place selection with ~24 per node), keep threads at 48, and run the A/B from a cold page cache so first-touch faults interleave the resident GGUF working set across both nodes' memory. Premise: the current placement pins threads to cores 0-47 (one node), capping streaming at the measured half-screen ceiling of 275-282 GB/s, while the same 48 threads at a full-screen spread measured ~410 GB/s. Dense Q8_0 MUL_MAT (40.6% of wall at ~213 GB/s = 77% of the 282 cap) and MUL_MAT_ID (36.3% at 82-94% of cap) are bandwidth-bound, so lifting the effective ceiling 1.46x should yield a double-digit tok/s gain. Distinct from the settled negatives: not the repack interleave (no CPU_REPACK pages under GGML_IQK=1; this places the original GGUF pages via first-touch) and not the localalloc source-flag treatment (no source change; OMP_PLACES is an installed recipe env key).

In DequantizerIQ3S's prepare overloads, replace calls to SignHelper::sign_4_values with four directly loaded 32-bit sign masks and AVX512VL masked byte subtraction. Leave the shared SignHelper, codebook lookup, quant selection and dot accumulation unchanged. This removes repeated shuffle/compare/sign-vector construction from IQ3_S expert dequantization. Masked subtraction must preserve the existing byte-negation behavior, including -128. CPU profiles are unavailable; no timing attribution or gain is claimed. The existing shared-helper comment warns that a similar implementation slowed TG, so this private specialization is an explicitly uncertain hypothesis under the selected MTP-d4 launch and required ppl-contract gates.

In the cpu_fa_schedule route, interleave two query heads sharing one KV head for each query position: traverse KV cells once and update separate per-head attention accumulators using the existing K/V reads and arithmetic. Partition these head pairs across threads, retaining the existing paths for use_ref, split-KV and tiled prefill. This targets repeated mask traversal and K/V access at 64k depth, rather than the exhausted matmul-prelude/barrier mechanisms. HEAD already skips fully masked runs; this proposal reuses traversal across heads. It is bit-exact by construction because each output row still processes the same surviving KV cells in ascending order with the same dot, exp and accumulator sequence, including the existing hybrid-precision fallback. CPU profiles at short and long depth are unavailable, so no sampled hotspot or gain is claimed.

In ggml_cpu_try_fuse_ops at inspected HEAD 511f4b637baa, fuse a contiguous F32 RMS_NORM with its sole F16 MUL_MAT consumer using shape-general type, layout, use-count and scratch-capacity checks. Split K across the team with remainder handling; compute partial sums of squares and weight-input dots, then reduce in fixed thread order and apply normalization. Use the skipped norm output as cache-line-separated partial storage, with overlap checks, rather than persistent mutable state or cached results. Finish input reads before writing the final output. This is TOL, not bit-exact to HEAD. It attacks hc_mixes underutilization and repeated passes without the previously regressing tile-plan change. The sampled synchronization fraction motivates examining work balance but is not a gain estimate; no serving gain is presumed.

At inspected HEAD 511f4b637baa, replace the unfused RMS_NORM body's memcpy followed by ggml_vec_scale_f32 with one loop writing y[i] = x[i] * scale. Preserve the existing eight-double-chain reduction, scale calculation, row ownership, strides and fused branch. Complete the full reduction before any write, including in-place cases. Outputs remain bit-identical by construction; the mechanism removes one output-buffer pass without barriers or workspace. Synchronization is parked and current bandwidth evidence discourages further quantized-dot instruction shaving, motivating this smaller mechanism. RMS_NORM has 3.02% sibling wall share, not an estimated gain; the achievable serving effect may be below the floor.

target_symbol: tinyBLAS_Q0_AVX<block_q8_0, block_q8_0, float>::gemm4xN (RN=2/3 specializations, body at :1524)
statement: Answers the rejection: the verify batch is N=3, which is exactly why this hypothesis targets gemm4xN<3> — the N=3 kernel itself (23.93% of sampled periods; dense MUL_MAT ≈ 40% of decode cycle, operator correction-2's largest kernel lever) — instead of the sync path. Mechanism: the inner k-loop of tinyBLAS_Q0_AVX::gemm4xN (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/llamafile/sgemm.cpp:1524, admitted dense_q8_tinyblas route) processes one 34-byte Q8_0 block (fp16 d + 32 qs) per iteration. Anchor disassembly (libggml-cpu.so.0 0x23d950, gemm4xN<3>) shows ~111 instructions per block: ~25 are per-block shared overhead — 4 d-word loads + shift/or + vcvtph2ps, 3 fp16-table B-delta lookups + vperm2f128, loop add/cmp/jne, and one spilled accumulator (vfmadd213ps + vmovaps at [rsp-0x20]) — and only 4 A-block loads (136 B) are in flight per iteration (B loads are already CSE'd). At 48 threads, 136 B/block is only ~24-26 ns of per-thread DRAM time (anchor 254 GB/s compute on the full screen = 62% of the 410 GB/s ceiling; ~92% of the 275.3 GB/s half-screen ceiling), so the loop runs at the issue-pressure/DRAM intersection, not DRAM-bound. Edit (body-only): explicitly 2x-unroll the k-loop inside gemm4xN so one iteration processes blocks l and l+1 (pointer step 0x44), sharing loop control, halving per-block delta-pack/loop/spill overhead, and doubling in-flight A loads to 272 B; per-block code (same load/updot/madd calls) stays unchanged, odd-k keeps a single-block tail. Per-output f32 term order is unchanged (terms still arrive in block order l, l+1, ... via the identical madd sequence), so outputs are bit-identical by construction — no rowexact/expert-flip risk. Priced honestly: dense = 40% of cycle; a ~15-20% muop reduction per A byte buys up to ~2-3.5% of cycle if issue-bound, null if DRAM-bound on the A/B screen.

Extend ggml_cpu_try_fuse_ops with a guarded RMS_NORM -> MUL_MAT fusion for contiguous F32 inputs and narrow F16 weights, including hc_mixes [20480,24] at nt=1-3. Use a new static helper to partition K across the thread team, accumulate partial sum-of-squares and weight-input dots, then combine partials in a fixed order and apply normalization to the outputs. Require a sole-consumer intermediate and fall back for unsupported layouts. Source inspection confirms this graph currently materializes normalized activations and only RMS_NORM+MUL is fused. This targets work balance and per-node fixed cost, the highest sampled unresolved family, while avoiding further bandwidth-bound dot-loop shaving and the regressed tile-plan changes. It removes normalized-buffer materialization and F32-to-F16 activation conversion and distributes long reductions across workers. This is TOL, not bit-exact: split-K and normalization after the dot change arithmetic.

Change only float tinyBLAS::matmul's tile plan when 2 <= n <= 5 and the existing plan exposes fewer jobs than threads. In the m%8 branch use mnpack<4,1,1> with SIZE_N=1 and BN=1: at nth=48,N=5, Q38FN ssm_alpha/ssm_beta F32 [2560 -> 48] grow from 6 to 60 jobs, and indexer.k_proj BF16 [2560 -> 128] grows from 16 to 160 jobs when AVX512BF16 is enabled. In the m%4 branch use mnpack<1,1,1> with SIZE_N=1 and BN=1: hc_attn_inject/hc_ffn_inject F32 [10240 -> 4] grow from 1 to 20 jobs. Preserve other plans, including already adequately populated nodes. This recovers idle threads on the served N=5 verify path; N=1 MTP graphs and Q8_0 hc_down nodes are unaffected. Column groups re-read A, so added parallelism may lose to reduced reuse. BE-order by construction: each output retains the identical increasing-k madd chain and hsum; only tile grouping and thread ownership change. The 34.12% sampled synchronization-family fraction motivates work balance but is not removable wall time; the sibling's 31.40% MUL_MAT wall share does not establish these nodes' individual contribution.

Declared runtime arm load-threads-48: loader reader team = the 48 compute threads, so no smaller OpenMP team precedes compute and libgomp workers spin on stale places; Q38FN is sync/spin-bound (~17% of the readbw ceiling), the same mechanism class. Load-time only.

In the inspected HEAD 74ee5c5027cc rms_norm template, replace the sequential sum-of-squares chain with eight independent double accumulators, combine them in a fixed order, and handle the scalar tail. Preserve float multiplication before promotion, row ownership, strides, full summation before in-place writes, and fused scaling. This breaks the serial addition dependency without workspace changes or barriers. It is TOL, not bit-exact to HEAD. Re-propose the previously patch-rejected mechanism with only the body hunk, preserving the EOF blank line. Synchronization proposals have unresolved coverage or settled negative evidence, and current bandwidth evidence retires matmul instruction shaving. RMS_NORM contributes 2.96% of sibling wall; its achievable serving gain may remain below the floor.

In ggml_cpu_node_is_solo, after the existing F32 checks and before the row guards, admit SUM_ROWS, CLAMP and DIV when both destination and src0 have at most 256 elements, retaining the existing destination cap. Source inspection confirms the MoE normalization sequence SUM_ROWS -> CLAMP -> DIV in llama-graph.cpp. At verify widths 2-3, admitting all three creates an actual consecutive solo run and removes two graph publication barriers per occurrence. SUM_ROWS already runs exclusively on thread 0; CLAMP and DIV retain their per-element arithmetic when executed with nth=1. Thread 0 executes dependencies in graph order, and the existing closing barrier publishes every result before other workers resume, making this bit-exact by construction. This targets the highest-ranked synchronization/work-balance family (34.78% sampled user-cycle attribution, not a wall share or predicted gain), avoids the rejected isolated-CLAMP no-op, and does not repeat the exhausted dense-Q8 seed family. The saved barriers may still be insufficient to clear the serving floor.

In ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat, flatten the existing shared activation-quantization work across all (activation row, quant block) pairs instead of assigning each thread the same block stripe separately in every row. For small verify batches, this distributes otherwise idle block stripes across the 48-thread team and can shorten the prelude before the existing barrier. Preserve mm_batch1, scratch layout, dispatch, and dot kernels. This is bit-exact by construction: each quant block uses the same from_float operation on the same input bytes, and each output dot retains its reduction order. This addresses work balance in the highest-ranked sampled family; the sampled synchronization fraction is not a predicted gain.

At inspected HEAD c40c7d18, the non-tiled F16 attention scheduler initializes a shared chunk counter, crosses a team barrier, and dynamically claims row chunks. For non-reference, non-split-KV decode/verify with N<=8 and at least nth query rows, assign each thread one balanced contiguous row range and call _one_chunk once, bypassing that counter and barrier. This removes scheduling and repeated helper setup without additional scratch. BE by construction: only row ownership changes; every row retains its original ascending KV traversal, dot products, softmax updates, overflow replay and sink handling. Preserve use_ref, tiled, split-KV and other shapes. This targets synchronization overhead within the observed 4.40% attention wall share; the larger solo/slab/dot mechanisms are exhausted, and no gain is inferred from sampled libgomp cycles.

In ggml_cpu_node_is_solo in ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c, raise only CONCAT's src[1] row limit from 3 to 5, retaining the existing F32, source/output row and element-count guards. HEAD already admits five-row solo nodes but CONCAT retains a three-row exception. This lets eligible MTP-d4 verify CONCAT nodes join existing thread-0 solo runs, avoiding intervening team synchronization. It addresses the highest-ranked unresolved synchronization/work-balance family; its actual payoff remains unmeasured. Bit-exact by construction: CONCAT copies the same elements, and the existing solo-run boundary publishes them before parallel consumers execute.

In ggml_iqk_try_mul_mat_id's multi-row branch (ids->ne[1] >= 2, i.e. the N=3 serving verify; the single-token mmid_batch1 slab is gated on ids->ne[1]==1 and never runs there), the used experts are dispatched as one iqk_mul_mat_moe(..., Ny=cne1, ith, nth) call per expert, so every thread re-runs MulMat::prepare and re-partitions each expert 1/nth into a thin ~ne01/nth row stripe, ~n_groups times per op. When every used expert is routed exactly one activation row (cne1==1, the common verify case: 3 tokens rarely collide on one expert; groups with cne1>1 keep the existing call), apply the flat (expert,row) slab partition that the single-token path already uses: build group starts over the already-built matrix_rows map, set units_total = (ne01/slab_gran)*n_groups, hand thread ith the contiguous unit range [units_total*ith/nth, units_total*(ith+1)/nth) and dispatch each segment via iqk_mul_mat_moe_rows(..., Ny=1, ...). Each thread then streams one long contiguous run of one expert's weight rows (crossing at most two adjacent expert slabs) and pays prepare/tile setup O(1) instead of once per expert, removing the per-expert 1/nth stripe overhead that the B3-k keep already measured and removed for the single-token path. Bit-identical: with cne1==1 the kernel is Ny=1 funcs[0] before and after (is_dequant_better(Q4_K,1)==Q4_K), DataInfo/row_mapping are built identically, each output row accumulates over the same blocks in the same order independent of the computing thread or 64-row tile boundary, and dst rows stay disjoint per (id, token).

In the cpu_fa_schedule route, interleave two query heads sharing a KV head inside one ascending KV-cell walk for non-tiled F16 attention, only when enough (head-pair, query-row) tasks exist to occupy the team. Q38FN verify N=5 supplies 60 such tasks for 48 threads. Reuse each cell's K/V cache lines across the pair while retaining separate query conversions, softmax state and accumulators within existing scratch. Preserve the original use_ref, tiled and split-KV paths. This is BE-order: each output row retains exactly its original KV order and dot/exp/update sequence. The current attention wall share is only 1.88%; this lower-ranked proposal addresses the explicitly admitted long-context surface, whose Q38FN performance remains unmeasured, rather than claiming a large frozen-request gain.

In ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat, for Q8_0 weights with contiguous F32 activations, 2-8 total activation rows and rowexact batching disabled, redundantly quantise all rows into each worker's grow-on-demand static _Thread_local scratch and attempt the existing quantised llamafile dispatch without the shared-conversion barrier. Eligibility depends only on team-shared tensor properties and configuration; allocation failure is fatal via GGML_ASSERT, never a per-thread fallback. Scratch is overwritten every call, has no pointer key and is not an activation cache. Allocate ne11*ne12*ne13*row_size bytes and preserve HEAD's (i12*ne11+i13*ne12*ne11)*row_size B offsets. If llamafile declines, all workers initialise/publish current_chunk through the existing team barrier before the generic chunk loop; the nth>=nchunk0*nchunk1 restriction is unnecessary for the successful static tinyBLAS path. Leave width 1's mm_batch1 path unchanged. Every dense Q8_0 N=5 node is eligible, including hc_attn_down and hc_ffn_down [10240->320]; BF16/F16 paths remain unchanged. This targets fixed prelude synchronization within the 31.73% MUL_MAT wall-share family, not the sampled libgomp fraction as a gain estimate. The price is full conversion per worker: 50 KiB of F32 input at K=2560,N=5 and 200 KiB at K=10240,N=5, versus approximately 1/48 of that work in HEAD. Scratch high-water size is 8*K*34/32 bytes, 87,040 bytes at K=10240. Expected gain is uncertain because redundant conversion may outweigh the removed barrier. BE-order: Q8_0 conversion is independent per block, so whole-row conversion produces identical bytes; tile ownership, accumulation order and stores remain unchanged, and MUL_MAT output does not alias src1. The added static mutable TLS scratch is expected to trigger the integrity screen's hot_path_mutable_state flag.

In ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat, extend the barrier-free condition to multi-row inputs when src1->type already equals vec_dot_type and nth >= nchunk0*nchunk1. Source inspection shows these cases publish no converted activation bytes and never read current_chunk, yet HEAD still initializes that counter and executes a team barrier. Removing this unnecessary synchronization preserves each output's vec_dot arithmetic and reduction order bit-exactly. CPU sampled attribution is unavailable; the sibling's 31.45% MUL_MAT wall share motivates testing but does not establish this subpath's cost or an expected gain. Preserve the selected CPU launch and MTP-d4 requests.

Default-enable iqk_q8_0_enabled() (body at ggml/src/ggml-cpu/iqk/iqk_dispatch.cpp:58-64; today true only when GGML_IQK_Q8_0 is set) so dense Q8_0 MUL_MAT nodes — the dominant decode kernel, tinyBLAS_Q0_AVX gemm4xN<1..3>, ~40% of decode wall at ~254 GB/s compute vs ~410 GB/s ceiling — are routed to the iqk Q8_0 path: F32 activations quantized in-graph to Q8_2_X4 (symmetric 8-bit, 16-element scale grid, (n/32)*36 B/row) and computed by the registered x86 kernels (mul_mat_qX_0_q8_2_Tx for N=1/2/4, mul_mat_qX_1_q8_2_T for N=3/5/6/7, kMaxQ fallback; iqk_gemm_legacy_quants.cpp:3424-3428) on ymm-dpbusd + offset-trick. Engagement preconditions verified in-tree: iqk_typeA_supported(Q8_0)=true (iqk_dispatch.cpp:131), iqk_shape_supported(Q8_0,*)=true (:175-179), and the wsize guard (:257) compares against the graph-max work buffer (ggml-cpu.c:4362) which in every verify graph is reserved by MUL_MAT_ID nodes at Q8_K activation size (ggml-cpu.c:3455, >=1.25 B/elem > Q8_2_X4's 1.125 B/elem), so main-model dense nodes pass; the same gate also captures any Q8_0 MUL_MAT_ID experts via the MMID hook (:394). Numerics: the activation grid changes from tinyBLAS's Q8_0 (32-element symmetric scale) to Q8_2_X4 (16-element symmetric scale), so outputs are NOT bit-identical to the champion — this must be accepted and is bounded by the route's scalar Q8_0 fixture gate plus the model-level gate. Prior: operator note 41 ranks this #0 on the GEMM ladder (stale-epoch architect bench, +58% decode on a Q8_0 model, n=1). Principal risk: the iqk kernel is 256-bit (ymm) dpbusd while the incumbent gemm4xN<3> is a tuned 512-bit (zmm) loop already carrying the 2x-unroll, tb-prefetch and offset-vnni keeps; the A/B decides whether the iqk loop structure (leaner fp epilogue, Q8_2_X4 B layout) wins at N=2..3.

In ggml_cpu_node_is_solo, allow noncontiguous F32 CPY/CONT/DUP nodes through the existing five-row and element-count bounds, preserving all other guards. Source inspection shows these copies currently terminate solo runs solely because of the contiguity check. Running bounded strided copies on thread 0 could join adjacent solo runs and remove team barriers, addressing the highest-ranked synchronization family. CPY accounts for 8.72% of sibling graph wall, but the eligible fraction is unknown. Bit-exact by construction: retain the existing copy kernels and graph order, with one worker completing each copy before its consumer.

Inside ggml_iqk_try_mul_mat_id, change only IQ3_S multi-token slab ownership at ids->ne[1]=2..5 from equal row units to cost-weighted units w(cne1)=10+cne1. Source inspection confirms IQ_N shares dequantizer preparation across activation columns; the rejected cne1 weighting overcorrected because it ignored that dominant shared work. The integer 10:1 estimate follows the supplied IQ3_S preparation versus per-column instruction counts. Compute cumulative expert costs from the existing matrix_row_counts, map shared thread boundaries back to slab_gran row units, and use identical rounding at adjacent boundaries for complete, disjoint coverage. Preserve every-thread kernel-selection checks and all fallbacks. Leave widths 6..8, IQ4_XS and DS41 Q4_K/Q5_K on HEAD's equal-unit partition; no cost constants are assumed for those types. This targets expert compute imbalance, not barrier removal. It is BE-order: activation bytes, selected kernel and each output's reduction order remain unchanged. No served ids census was available, so no measured makespan or gain is claimed. Illustratively, the critic's inferred mean multiplicity 1.25 and maximum 2 give costs 11.25 versus 12 under ideal weighted versus equal ownership, before granularity and boundary costs. The 26.35% MUL_MAT_ID wall share supports testing this bounded correction, but does not predict its gain.

In `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ops.cpp:ggml_compute_forward_rms_norm_f32` the parallelism domain is rows only (`for (int64_t i01 = ith; i01 < ne01; i01 += nth)` at :4115), so the ~2 norm ops per layer are executed by at most `min(ne01, nth)` threads: at decode N=1 only 1 of 48 threads participates and at speculative verify N=3 only 3 of 48 participate, leaving the rest of each call serialized behind one row's full scalar sum/reduce plus scale/mul store over ne00. Extend the partition to columns as well when `ne01 < nth`: give each thread a contiguous column-block of length `ceil(ne00 / ceil(nth/ne01))` for every row it co-owns, reduce the squared-sum in a fixed contiguous-block order (deterministic tree by block index, `bsum = bsum + block_sum` in ascending block order), publish the per-row `scale` via a per-row slot, then run the element-wise scale (or fused `x*scale*w`) over the same blocks. This turns the norm nodes from row-serial into row+column-parallel across all threads, shrinking the serial fraction of the graph (RMS_NORM ~3.17% of sampled cycles) without touching the exhausted local quant/dot or barrier families.

Extend ggml_cpu_try_fuse_ops with a static fused helper for single-consumer RMS_NORM followed by contiguous F16-weight MUL_MAT at the hc_mixes shape [20480,24], nt=1..3. Partition K across the thread team; each thread computes double-accumulated partial sums of squares and F16-weight/F32-input dot products, then reduce partials in fixed thread order and apply the RMS scale including epsilon. Use existing work storage with capacity checks and retain the unfused fallback. Source inspection confirms build_hc_mixes constructs this pair and HEAD only fuses RMS_NORM with MUL. This attacks narrow-M work imbalance and removes intermediate normalization writes, F16 activation conversion and separate dispatches. It differs from the regressed tile replans by changing data flow and distributing K. This is TOL, not bit-exact: reduction order and activation rounding change. The 32.72% synchronization sampled-cycle attribution motivates reducing idle work, but is not a gain estimate; sibling wall shares likewise establish opportunity only. Dense and expert instruction shaving is retired by the latest bandwidth evidence.

In tinyBLAS_Q0_AVX::gemm4xN, replace ceil-sized thread duties with proportional contiguous tile ranges: start=tiles*ith/nth and end=tiles*(ith+1)/nth. The inspected code can leave almost half the team idle when the tile count is just above a multiple of 48; proportional partitioning distributes those tiles across the team and reduces straggler wait.
